top_choice_rationale: Cărtărescu (P001) remains my choice on the common literary criteria. His voice is distinctive and recognizable, and his formal ambition is sustained across very large prose structures (Blinding and Solenoid, as publicly known). Memory, the body and dream are built into one continuing imaginative project, which gives the oeuvre depth beyond ornamental density. The case spans decades and does not rest on a single book. The proposal's citation scope is also sound: it centres on prose and leaves poetry as context, since translation coverage of the poetry is thinnest. The main unresolved risk is whether the later long fictions develop the earlier architecture or restate it. My provisional reading is that Solenoid changes the mode of the project, but this rests on public description and translation, not close reading of the Romanian. Agreement among the six round-2 files is correlated reasoning from shared public knowledge and is not evidence of merit. P000 is ranked below P001 because the case, though provisional, is the strongest available on the supplied record, and no award would withhold recognition on an unresolved question I cannot settle here.
